subject: [PATCH v2 02/18] xfs: convert iomap ops to ->iomap_next()

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Reviewer Christoph Hellwig expressed strong opposition to using variable number or argument macros, citing difficulties in understanding and generating compiler warnings due to misuse.
reviews.raw_body:
Don't go there.  These variable number or argument macros are a
complete pain to undestand and generate horrible compiler warnings
whenever someone messes up their first attempt at writing some
code (guess who never gets the first pass right? :))

reviews.author: Darrick Wong
reviews.summary: Reviewer Darrick Wong expressed confusion about the implementation of ->iomap_next() in xfs_iomap.c, specifically mentioning that he barely understands the subtlety in __define_iomap_end(), and labeled it as 'fugly'.
reviews.raw_body:
I /did/ label that as 'fugly'; I barely understand the subtlety that
goes on in __define_iomap_end. :)

--D

2026-07-03.patch_summary: This patch converts the iomap operations for XFS to use the new ->iomap_next() callback, which is a more efficient and flexible way of handling I/O mappings. The conversion uses the iomap_process() helper function to finish previous mappings and produce the next one. This change does not introduce any functional changes but rather updates the internal implementation of XFS's iomap operations. The patch affects several files in the fs/xfs directory, including xfs_file.c and xfs_iomap.c.
